Fifteen seconds later order-service reported a 95% miss ratio and started loading everything from Postgres (#69). This cache stampede pushed Postgres to 491/500 connections and 94–98% CPU (#74, #79). Simple primary-key SELECTs on orders slowed to 2.5–8s (#75, #99, #114), order-service queries timed out after 5s (#84, #108), and the gateway returned 504s on /checkout starting at 20:10 (#78, #88, ...). The trigger, losing the cache, would have been survivable alone; the damage came from every miss hitting the database at once. The card-processor connection reset at 20:03 (#33) succeeded on retry and happened before onset, so it is a red herring.
Postgres hit its connection and CPU limits. But this was caused by the cache-miss load, not by the resource being too small on its own.
Postgres queries timing out is the direct cause of the 504s, but Postgres was slow because of the stampede.

verdict.recommendedAction: Warm the Redis cache, or rate-limit and coalesce cache fills (single-flight / request coalescing) in order-service. Temporarily shed or throttle /checkout load until Postgres CPU and connection counts recover. Afterwards, turn on Redis persistence or replication so a node replacement doesn't come back empty, and add stampede protection.
